PullRequest.Title: artifacts: Add the GitHub pull request integration
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Add the first built-in artifact integration for explicitly recorded GitHub pull requests.

- Present open/draft/closed/merged state, checks, unresolved review threads, and merge readiness.
- Provide guarded repair prompts and native mark-ready/merge actions, with separate opt-in automation.
- Keep manual prompts in the invoking chat and automatic prompts in the trusted originating chat; recheck the checkout, head, permissions, account, and consent before effects.
- Retain same-head state during overlapping refreshes without enabling stale actions. Keep list icons present and sort checks as running, failing, skipped, then passed.
- Support scoped repository-client leases, same-token reauthorization, and workspace-specific check exclusions for automatic mark-ready without relaxing merge requirements.
- Reuse shared GitHub credential/feedback helpers and include the complete architecture documentation.
- Keep integrations behind the application-scoped, default-off `chat.artifactIntegrations.enabled` setting. Enabling integrations suppresses Agent Merge without rewriting its saved preference; disabling pauses integrations and cancels only their automatic work while retaining saved opt-ins, activity, and ordinary artifact links.

The provider does not use Agent Merge's controller, configuration, or elevated permission mode. Other extensions contribute through the generic API from layer 2.

## Stack

This is **4 of 4**, based on #343003.

| Order | PR | Base |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | #343002 - Shared integration runtime | `main` |
| 2 | #343001 - Agent host, extension API, and agent tools | #343002 |
| 3 | #343003 - Generic artifact UI | #343001 |
| 4 | **#343000 - GitHub pull request integration (this PR)** | #343003 |

This completes the replacement for #337678 and #338107. The final stack was checked against the preserved upstream-integrated source tree; the separate ExP extension is not included or modified by the restack.

**Safety:** validation used synthetic resources and mocked GitHub responses. No real PR was merged, marked ready, or otherwise mutated; no live repair prompt or automation consent was submitted.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed trigger, complete call path, subprocess implementation, polling cadence, and all-chat concurrency are directly visible in repository code. Exact latency varies with repository size and chat count, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Git subprocesses and working-tree filesystem I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For every integrated pull request, each snapshot transition or broad session/chat/config event schedules a scan of every chat; each matching checkout executes five uncached Git commands (branch, remote, rev-parse, status, branch) per working directory, with all chats run through Promise.all. Multiple PR artifacts multiply this fan-out, and a new event can start another async scan before the prior one finishes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated subprocess bursts and repository scans increase CPU/filesystem load, contend with the agent's own Git operations, and can delay artifact automation/action availability in sessions with several chats or recorded pull requests.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no GitHub pull-request artifact binding and therefore no event-driven all-chat checkout scan on live pull-request polling or chat lifecycle changes.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new autorun reads both the live pull-request snapshot and a broad hostChanges signal, then schedules refreshWorkspaces; that method maps every session chat concurrently and calls checkout, which crosses multiple Git subprocess boundaries.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `resource.snapshot.read(reader); this.hostChanges.read(reader); refreshWorkspace.schedule();` at lines 347-349 newly places a full all-chat checkout scan behind every PR snapshot and broad host event; the same added class performs the unbounded `Promise.all(...chats.map(...checkout))` fan-out.
Findings.Title: Stop rescanning every chat checkout on each pull-request update
Findings.Impact: With integrations enabled, an active multi-chat session causes background Git bursts whenever any PR fragment enters loading/ready (background checks can poll every 60 seconds, interactive checks every 15 seconds) and on turn/pending-message/session events. Ten eligible chats can launch roughly 50 Git processes for one scan of one PR, before overlapping scans or additional PRs, causing noticeable CPU/I/O spikes and slower agent Git work.
Findings.Evidence: Lines 347-349 subscribe checkout refresh to every resource.snapshot and hostChanges update. hostChanges includes ChatTurnStarted/Complete/Cancelled, pending-message, session metadata/chat events, and all root/session config changes. refreshWorkspaces at lines 644-651 uses Promise.all over every chat. checkout at lines 609-629 invokes getCurrentBranchName twice, getFetchRemoteUrls, revParse, and hasUncommittedChanges; AgentHostGitService implements each via child_process.execFile('git', ...), except the repository-root lookup after its cache is warm. PullRequestResourceService commits separate loading/ready snapshot updates for core, checks, review threads, and mergeability and polls pending background checks every 60s. RunOnceScheduler only coalesces the 50ms timer; its callback does not await refreshWorkspaces, so later events can overlap an in-flight scan while workspaceRevision merely discards stale results.
Findings.Recommendation: Refresh only checkout state that is actually needed: lazily validate the invoking chat for manual actions and the origin chat when a checkout-dependent automation is enabled. If per-chat action availability must stay live, cache/dedupe by working-directory plus relevant head/ref, invalidate only on chat workspace or Git-state changes, serialize/cancel stale scans, and put Git probes behind a shared concurrency limit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Display and live-update recorded GitHub pull-request artifacts in the active session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial model acquisition, credential resolution, and the core GitHub response must complete before the pill can show authoritative PR state; checks/reviews/mergeability fill in independently. Later polling is off the basic interaction critical path, while opening details promotes polling cadence and keeps updates on the visible-details path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub credential/account identity and subscribe to/fetch PR core, review threads with bodies, required and optional checks, and mergeability.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One pooled observer per effective PR/account/runtime key; four fragment families poll at background cadences of 60-300 seconds, or interactive cadences of 15-60 seconds while details are leased.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base had the generic integration framework but no built-in GitHub pull-request artifact integration or its PR network observer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Credential/core fetch blocks authoritative initial state; other fragments progressively enable sections/actions. Subsequent polling updates visible state but generally does not block chat interaction.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is unique pull-request resource plus authority/runtime/account after ArtifactResourcePool coalescing. Different recorded PRs, accounts, authorities, or runtime scopes create independent observers; duplicate bindings to the same pooled resource share the GitHub subscription.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: PullRequestResourceService schedules each fragment independently through its request scheduler. An authoritative refresh fetches core first, then reviewThreads, checks, and mergeability concurrently. Opening details changes the shared subscription from background to interactive priority rather than creating another subscription.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ArtifactResourcePool coalesces creation by authority, target host, runtime, canonical PR key, and credential scope. PullRequestResourceService also shares entries by normalized PR/account, retains dormant entries for 120 seconds, and uses transport ETags/credential caching; warm polls still cross the network but avoid duplicate same-key observers.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: match/createResource, resource pooling, subscription interests, polling policy, and query boundaries were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual request duration and number of simultaneously recorded PRs vary by repository and user workflow; pooling materially reduces duplicate same-PR calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: network work is intrinsic to the feature, keyed/coalesced by canonical resource and credential scope, lifecycle-owned, and polling is priority-aware.

Scenarios.Scenario: Keep checkout-dependent repair and automation availability current for a live PR artifact
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Checkout state gates repair actions and checkout-dependent automation; basic PR title/check presentation does not need it. The changed code nevertheless starts verification whenever any PR snapshot or broad host/config event changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run Git repository/branch/remote/HEAD/status probes to validate each chat checkout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: On a matching warm-cache checkout: branch, remote -v, rev-parse HEAD, status --porcelain, and branch again per chat/directory. All chats run concurrently for each binding and may be rescanned multiple times during one fragmented PR refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No built-in PR artifact binding performed event-driven all-chat Git validation in the base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The scan gates action/automation availability and can contend with agent Git operations; it is unnecessary for basic live PR presentation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost grows as integrated PR bindings × chats in the session × working directories examined × snapshot/chat/config event frequency. A successful first directory performs five uncached Git commands after repository-root cache warm-up.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Every binding uses Promise.all across all session chats with no shared limiter. RunOnceScheduler coalesces only a 50ms timer and does not await the async scan, so later events can overlap prior scans; independent PR bindings also run concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: AgentHostGitService caches repository-root resolution in an LRU, but branch, remote, HEAD, dirty-status, and final branch checks are executed anew on every scan. Workspace results are not keyed by directory/head for reuse; workspaceRevision only prevents stale result publication.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: changed event wiring, all-chat Promise.all, concrete AgentHostGitService execFile calls, and fragment polling/update cadence were all traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Sessions differ in chat count, directory count, repository size, and Git status latency; large worktrees and multi-chat sessions amplify the proven mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression submitted: broad events cause repeated, uncapped Git subprocess fan-out unrelated to the minimum state that changed.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run manual repair, mark-ready, merge, and opt-in automation actions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Manual and automatic code actions authoritatively refresh PR state before preparation and again immediately before mutation; repair prompts also validate the selected checkout before dispatch. These checks are intentionally on the action safety critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively refresh PR fragments and perform mark-ready, prepare-merge, merge, or enqueue mutations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one core plus three fragment refreshes per authoritative check, followed by the selected bounded mutation path; retries are occurrence-keyed and attempt-limited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: These artifact-specific actions did not exist in the base.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly blocks action preparation/execution to ensure current authorization, head, and merge state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate invoking/origin checkout before repair prompts and unchanged-only automatic merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequential directory probes until a matching checkout is found; one selected action/run at a time per resource/integration lane.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No artifact action used this checkout-validation path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks prompt dispatch or unchanged-only merge as a safety prerequisite.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One run acts on one PR resource. Prompt previews are bounded to 20 threads × 5 comments × 1,000 body characters or 100 failed checks. Execution lanes serialize by resource and integration; automation evaluation dispatches at most one applicable action before returning.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The shared executor serializes conflicting work by resource and integration keys. Within one authoritative refresh, core precedes three parallel fragment refreshes. Checkout probes for an invoked action are sequential within directories, and automatic evaluation has a running/pending coalescer.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The pooled resource and credential client are reused, but authoritative refresh deliberately supersedes/cancels stale fragment operations. Occurrence keys and durable run records prevent duplicate automation; retry attempts and previews are bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: action call paths, lane keys, bounds, and retry/coalescing rules were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: GitHub latency and repository status cost vary, but run cardinality and serialization are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: these boundaries are bounded, serialized, safety-critical, and use durable deduplication. The report concerns the same Git probes being eagerly repeated for all chats outside an invocation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable/disable artifact integrations and synchronize per-artifact workspace settings
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Changing the application setting immediately tears down active presentations/bridges, pauses automation, or restores retained bindings. Workspace check-exclusion changes dispatch metadata to the host; these operations are on the explicit setting-change path, not startup while disabled.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/write the existing artifact integration ledger while preserving consent and recording cancellations/restored bindings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One setting transition over retained bindings/runs; restore is sequential and disabled state does not instantiate integrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The ledger/storage boundary already existed; this diff adds enablement-driven retention and cancellation semantics.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Setting transition waits for initial enablement update during initialization; later updates are asynchronous and logged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch artifact-scoped workspace configuration to the Agent Host session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one dispatch per integrated artifact when chat/directory/ignored-check value or connection changes; structural equality suppresses unrelated configuration events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No PR-artifact workspace exclusion metadata was synchronized.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Automatic Mark Ready remains unavailable until settings arrive, but ordinary artifact presentation proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reacquire retained GitHub PR resources when integrations are re-enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Sequential per retained binding, with same-resource pooling once overlapping references exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No built-in PR artifact bindings existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Restored automation/live state waits for reacquisition; this follows explicit opt-in setting change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Restore cost scales with retained bindings that have enabled automation or unsettled/indeterminate runs and is processed sequentially. Workspace synchronization scales with integrated artifacts in the active session, with structural equality suppressing unchanged dispatches.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Binding restoration is a sequential loop. Automation cancellation uses Promise.all over currently unsettled automation runs but executor cancellation coalesces by run. Workspace sync emits at most one dispatch per changed artifact value and connection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Disabled integrations release models/resources while preserving ledger consent. Re-enable reacquires only retained bindings; resource pooling and GitHub credential caches apply. Workspace values retain lastValue/lastConnection and structural-dedupe repeats.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: enablement autoruns, retention predicate, sequential restore, cancellation, and workspace structural dedupe were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of retained automations is user-controlled but normally small; no unbounded history-wide restore was found.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: disabled mode is lazy, restore is bounded to retained bindings and sequential, and workspace IPC is deduplicated.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full changed-file inventory and relevant diff pages. One high-confidence boundary-fanout regression was reported: every PR snapshot/broad host event triggers uncapped all-chat Git checkout scans. Network observation, action execution, enablement lifecycle, pooling, paging, serialization, cleanup, and workspace synchronization were otherwise bounded or intentionally placed.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
